correctness.rationale: All proper ideals in a finite commutative square-zero local ring are exactly residue-field subspaces of the radical. Because any two proper ideals multiply to zero, exactly 1+k(L-2) of L^k ordered tuples have nonzero product. The comparison polynomial D_k(L) factors for k=2 and 3; D_4(3)=1 with strictly positive L-derivative for L>=3, and D_(k+1)=L D_k+2^k(L-2)(k(L-2)-1) proves all larger cases. Explicit eight-element rings are nonisomorphic by characteristic, and the standalone direct enumeration confirms each has six ideals and 27 zero-producing pairs; code is corroboration, not replacement for proof.

value.rationale: A recently posed field-characterization conjecture fails already for two explicit eight-element local nonfields, one characteristic two and one characteristic four. The complete Gaussian-binomial formula and exact equality/sign classification across all residue fields, radical ranks, and tuple lengths explain the failure structurally, proving that the field benchmark is neither a universal lower nor upper bound in this natural class. This is a motivated mathematical boundary result, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
